answer: The jury's own reward depends on rejecting low-quality answers, creating a shared incentive among honest graders to spot coordinated fakery, so a Sybil cluster collapses under the weight of its own low scores. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.
